mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE is below 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output and economic growth, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during four consecutive months of INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.5% in the same month signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise >= 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise by at least 0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly increase of at least 1% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise >= 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 and HOUST increase by at least 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 persons for five consecutive months signals strong labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >= 50,000 persons for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during five consecutive months of monthly PAYEMS gains >= 50,000.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the real retail sales series (RSAFS) and S&P 500 forward returns at the 5-day horizon: higher real retail sales signal near-term consumer confidence and spending, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly changes in RSAFS and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample walk-forward tests.
